CROW'S-NEST STAR-CHART STUDY — standing in the crow's-nest with a star-chart spread open between both hands, head tilted to read it, hair blowing across the paper, a meteor shower scribing silent white lines across the ink-blue sky above her

RIGGING SILHOUETTE — gripping a single thick rope at chest height with both hands, one foot braced against the hull, body at a diagonal lean away from the ship, hair arrowing straight down in the updraft, the full moon enormous and silver directly behind her head

CROW'S-NEST VIGIL AT GOLDEN HOUR — standing upright inside the crow's-nest with both forearms resting on the brass rail, a spyglass raised to one eye, her hair streaming sideways as amber light floods the cloudscape and the great silk envelope glows copper behind her

YARD-ARM STRADDLE IN MORNING MIST — seated astride the highest yard-arm with one knee hooked beneath the spar and both hands wrapped loosely around the mast, a sextant hanging from her belt, the airship cutting silently through pearl-grey fog below

BOWSPRIT WALK INTO STORM-LIGHT — balanced heel-to-toe along the bowsprit with arms spread wide for equilibrium, an astrolabe dangling from one raised fist, lightning blooming in violet thunderheads ahead as the prow cleaves into the oncoming front

STARBOARD SHROUD LEAN AT DUSK — hooked one arm through the starboard shroud and arching backward away from the rigging, head thrown back to face the sky, the other hand holding a signal-lantern aloft as the last crimson band of sunset ignites the cloud-floor

MAINMAST SUMMIT SILHOUETTE — arms folded across her chest at the very tip of the mainmast cap, feet planted on the iron cap-plate, every cloud in the hemisphere spread beneath her as the full moon rises enormous and silver directly behind her head

FORWARD RAIL COMMAND OVER CLOUDFALL — gripping the brass prow rail with both hands wide apart, leaning far out over the bow, her hair whipping forward, a star-chart pinned under one palm as the airship crests a cloudfall and the infinite blue abyss opens below

RATLINE CLIMB CAUGHT MID-REACH — frozen in motion three-quarters up the ratlines with one arm stretched high and one boot braced on a lower rung, glancing back over her shoulder toward the camera, dawn light raking across her from the east and the gondola hanging small below

PORT YARD-ARM TIP PERCH AT NOON — seated sideways on the very tip of the port yard-arm, legs dangling freely, holding a brass telescope extended toward the horizon, brilliant white cumulonimbus towers framing her on both sides in blazing midday light

MAST-TOP ARMS-WIDE TRIUMPH — standing at the topmast crosstrees with both arms flung wide and head tilted back, nothing above her but open stratosphere, the cloud-ocean rolling in every direction thousands of feet below, the ship's pennant cracking in the wind beside her

SIGNAL-LANTERN SWING ON AFT SHROUD — spinning on one heel while gripping the aft shroud, free arm extending a lit signal-lantern in a wide arc, the amber flame the only warm light in a cold blue twilight full of scattered cloud-islands

SEXTANT READING ON THE CATWALK — crouched on one knee on the upper catwalk with the sextant raised and one eye pressed to the arc, elbow resting on the catwalk rail, the sun blazing directly above and casting her short sharp shadow straight down into the void

FLARE-SIGNAL FROM THE CROW'S-NEST RIM — standing on the outer rim of the crow's-nest with heels hooked on the inside rail, leaning outward at a daring angle and firing a signal-flare overhead, a red comet streaking above her as storm-clouds boil on the horizon

BOWSPRIT TIP IN CLOUD-GLOW — standing upright on the very tip of the bowsprit with arms clasped behind her back, hair pouring forward in the slipstream, the airship plunging into a canyon of luminous cloud-walls that glow rose and gold around her

RIGGING HAMMOCK-HANG AT TWILIGHT — lying back across two parallel shroud-lines as if in a hammock, one leg dangling, one hand holding an open star-chart overhead, reading it against the last indigo light as the first stars appear above the cloud-deck

GUNWALE STAND IN ARCTIC LIGHT — balanced on the outer gunwale with one hand lightly touching the rigging and the other hanging free, gazing calmly at a horizon where the sun skims low and the cloudtops are lacquered gold and ice-blue

ASTROLABE ALOFT ON THE CROSSTREES — standing at the lower crosstrees with one arm raised high holding an astrolabe into the wind, the other hand braced on the mast, the ship banking into a long curve so the cloud-world tilts dramatically behind her
